sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Achillea millefolium is a rhizomatous perennial, usually 10–100 cm tall. Its alternate leaves are finely divided, and many small flower heads form a flat-topped cluster, usually white and sometimes pinkish. It is native across temperate and subarctic parts of Eurasia and is now widespread elsewhere, growing in meadows, open ground and roadsides.

sections.title: Food and toxicity
sections.text: The sources consulted do not establish a reliable food use for this species. The ASPCA lists yarrow as toxic to dogs, cats and horses; that veterinary warning should not be generalized to people.
